The fresh curfew runs from 2100 GMT Tuesday to 0400 GMT Wednesday and applies to the Republique public square in the city's central east, where many weekend clashes took place, and in the central les Halles district which is full of shops. title: Ukraine ‘losing people and time’, Zelensky says after Oslo talks
description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has wrapped up talks with US envoys in Norway Tuesday where he was determined to put diplomacy back on a "more constructive path”, Oslo officials said.  Zelensky told a post-meeting press briefing that Ukraine was not losing the war but was “losing people and time”, adding that he was hopeful moving forward because “we have some clear ideas of how to get peace”.

title: Zelensky meets Witkoff as US-Ukraine relations sink to new lows
description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was meeting US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Tuesday in a ​bid to rescue relations that have sunk to new lows as President Donald Trump has courted Moscow and Kyiv has complained about Washington withholding vital defences. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kharkiv.

title: Attack by Daesh-affiliated group in Mali kills 48 people
description: An attack by militants linked to the Islamic State in Mali’s Ménaka region resulted in 48 deaths, including children and the elderly, amid accusations against civilians of aiding the military.

title: Infantino set to take his FIFA re-election campaign to Japan to court Asian soccer federations
description: TOKYO: Gianni Infantino’s campaign for re-election as FIFA president is set to move this week to Japan and a meeting scheduled for Wednesday with the Asian Football Confederation. This comes after Infantino apologized last week in Zurich, Switzerland, to FIFA’s 37-member ruling council — which he chairs — for “mistakes” he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2 billion sell-off plan for the World Cup. title: Two men re-arrested for suspected spying for Iran in air base scare: UK police
description: UK police re-arrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iranian intelligence following a security scare at a US-used air base in the UK. The arrests involve a British citizen and a dual UK-Iranian national.

title: Iran says Iraq will expel exiled Kurdish opposition members
description: BAGHDAD: Iran’s ambassador to Iraq said on Tuesday that Baghdad had agreed to “expel” or hand over members of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups who have taken refuge on the Iraqi side of the border. The announcement came after senior Iraqi security officials repeatedly told AFP that Baghdad was refusing to do so, fearing for the lives of the Kurdish exiles. title: US VP Vance says staying out of Israel vote as Trump backs Netanyahu
description: US Vice President JD Vance stated he will not endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, opting to remain neutral in Israeli elections, unlike Donald Trump, who supports Netanyahu.

title: What F1’s return to Africa means for a continent long overlooked by global sports
description: Formula 1 announces a 10-year deal with Rwanda for an African Grand Prix, expected to boost the continent’s global sports profile despite criticism from human rights groups.

title: Rwanda tipped to host first European migrant return hub
description: Rwanda is expected to become the site of a return hub where certain EU countries intend to send migrants who have no right to stay in Europe. An agreement is being discussed and may be finalized as early as next month.
